His words (2026-11-18): "I think we should disable the switching altogether." He asked that it add no footprint to OrcaSlicer's files.

What this means for you:
- Build the page guard as the prototype has it: JusPrin binds `wxEVT_BOOKCTRL_PAGE_CHANGING` on the main window's notebook from `Shell/ShellController.cpp` and vetoes every page except Home, Prepare and Project while the JusPrin view is installed. Open no window in place of the refused page, for Preview, Device or any other.
- Keep this entirely in JusPrin's files. If you find you need any line in an OrcaSlicer-owned file for the guard, stop and tell Kenneth before writing it; he asked to be checked with first.
- In your report this is agreed, not a default. With my two earlier messages (changes dropped on a switch; every taken message goes to the chat), nothing in the handover's "Not agreed" section remains unagreed.
</cross-session-message>

input.content:
A filament switch saves its version before the slot changes

Kenneth requires that after a profile switch drops unsaved setting
changes, the person can get the project back exactly as it was just
before the switch (2026-11-18): "the user will be able to rewind to
everything right before the switch, even if the unsaved setting changes
were dropped."

A filament switch broke that. JusPrin's filament switch
(SetupCommands::select_filament_preset) runs the sidebar's sequence:
it renames the filament slot first, and only then asks the filament
page to switch, where "Transfer or discard changes" comes up. The
version saved at that question named the new filament with the old
filament's settings. Restoring it left the new filament selected with
the old one's settings loaded onto it as unsaved changes.

Now the filament switch saves the version itself before the slot
changes, through the same shared function, and refuses the switch if no
version can be saved. While that save is in effect
(OrcaMessages::SavedFirst), the question is answered without saving
again, so no newer half-switched version is made. The printer and
process switches ask before they change anything and need no change.

Tests: JusPrinShellHarness --orca-messages now rewinds after a filament
switch, a process switch, a printer switch with unsaved changes in the
printer, filament and process, and a project close. Each case opens
Version history in the left panel, finds the version the project was on
as the switch returned, presses its Restore button, and checks the
profiles, the changed values, which profiles hold unsaved changes and the
objects against the project just before. The filament case failed
before this change (Generic PETG selected with Bambu PLA Basic's
settings) and passes now. LeftPane::press_action takes which of several
rows with the same label to press: Version history labels each row with
the minute it was saved, so versions from one minute share a label.

content.text:
Commit `2fd84e0d03` makes a filament switch save its version before the switch starts. Without that, the version could not bring the project back as it was. The harness now checks Kenneth's rewind requirement after four kinds of switch or close. Nothing is merged or pushed.

**Page refusal (Kenneth's last open decision):** no code change was needed. JusPrin's own `ShellController` already refuses every page except Home, Prepare and Project, opens nothing in its place, and adds no line to OrcaSlicer's files. The report now lists it as agreed, so every default is agreed.

**Rewinding after a switch or close:**
- **What the checks do:** each case opens Version history in the left panel and presses Restore on the version from just before. It then compares the profiles, the changed values, which profiles have unsaved changes, and the objects.
- **Cases covered:**
  - a filament switch;
  - a process switch;
  - a printer switch with unsaved changes in the printer, filament and process;
  - closing the project, then reopening it from Home and carrying on.
- **Bug found and fixed:** JusPrin's filament switch renames the filament slot before OrcaSlicer asks "Transfer or discard changes". So the version saved at that question named the new filament but held the old filament's settings. Restoring it left Generic PETG selected with Bambu PLA Basic's settings on it.
  - The filament switch now saves the version before the slot changes, and the question that follows does not save a second time.
  - The filament case failed before the fix and passes now.

**What a person sees in Version history:** each row shows only the date and minute it was saved, plus a Restore button. Nothing marks a version as coming from a switch, and versions saved in the same minute look identical; in the test, seven rows all read "11/18/2026 18:30". The version from just before the switch is the top row once the app has saved after the switch. Until that next save the list leaves it out, because it still counts as the current version. Picture 8 in the notes folder shows this.

**Still open:**
- Every restore marks the printer as changed in two settings nobody touched:
  - `thumbnails` gains a space after a comma.
  - `machine_max_junction_deviation` reads the same text on both sides.

  This comes from loading the saved project, which this branch doesn't touch. Fixing it likely means changing OrcaSlicer-owned files, so it is listed rather than fixed.
- The commit messages of `2bd193ce5f` and `67fc1d450f` still say "Not agreed yet" about things Kenneth has since agreed. Rewording them changes their commit ids, so it needs his yes.

**Tests:**
- `--orca-messages` and nine other harness modes pass, and clang-tidy passes.
- `--printer-menu` passed 3 of 5 runs. Both failures came while another session's build had the machine's load near 30. The two runs at a load near 12 passed. The failing checks read the header's printer menu, which this commit doesn't touch, but I haven't proven the failures unrelated.

I updated the report in the shared notes folder (`orca-messages-report.md`) and sent this summary to the teammate session that relayed Kenneth's decisions.

Another Claude session sent a message:
<cross-session-message from="local_0556d7f7-94a8-41cf-a840-aa76d6268545" from-name="btw: So these are the settings changed to the printer or filame…">
Kenneth asks you to test what the AI model is sent on the next turn after a profile switch has dropped setting changes.

Why: Kenneth's assumption (2026-11-18) is that people do not set settings themselves, the AI sets them, so after a switch of printer or filament "the AI should guide the user from the new starting point". That only works if the request the model receives on the next turn shows the new printer or filament and the settings as they now are, and does not leave the model believing its earlier changes are still in effect.

The case to run, through the real app path, for a printer switch and for a filament switch:
1. In a project chat, have the AI change a setting that is about the object, not the printer (for example more walls for a stronger part), so the chat history holds that tool call and its result.
2. Switch the printer (then, separately, the filament) from the header, so the change is dropped with no question.

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered, with one
  exception below.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

Two kinds of change are ever answered, each only in a case that says so
(`later`), because what matters there is what the model does next: a
`setup_record` with a plan and no purpose (`print-this-no-purpose` and
`print-hook-no-purpose`), and a `slice_start` (`print-hook-no-purpose`). `later`
maps what the run has done so far to the point recorded right after it, by a
conversation that starts like the case's and does the same. The answer is the
result the app gave there, not a stand-in. Of a plan's result only the plan is the
model's own: its headline, decisions, unverified and risks take the place of the
scripted ones, as the app would echo them. Reads written before the call are
answered from the point the run is at; the call's result and every read after it
from the later point, whose reads were taken with the change in place. If the
response holds a second change, the case fails and nothing is answered. A plan that
names a purpose fails the same way. A slice of a plate the recording did not slice,
or an order of changes with no point in `later`, is unobserved. The response of an
answered change is not counted in `MAX_READS`, which counts responses of reads.

A slice ends after its turn, and the app then starts a new turn. So `later` also
names that turn, as "the slice's end". When the model's reply leaves the case
undecided while a slice runs, the run appends the model's reply and what the
recording appended after its own scripted reply (the workspace and "The slice of
Plate 1 finished."), and the next step decides. Reads there come from that point.
On the Claude CLI, whose run ends with the reply, this starts a new run from the
whole chat.

     - Ask before revert or amend.
     - No fix for an unreproduced bug.
     - Temporary files go in the scratchpad.
     - Never print the API keys in `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`.

   **Agreed decisions (Kenneth, 2026-11-18, relayed by teammate `local_0556d7f7-94a8-41cf-a840-aa76d6268545`)**
   - Closing a project and switching a profile share one save-first function. A failed save refuses the close or switch and reports the failure.
   - Changes are dropped on a switch.
   - Every taken message goes into the chat: "If there is an active chat, put that in the active chat, otherwise put that in the empty chat panel. We already have a way to do that."
   - Page refusal: "I think we should disable the switching altogether." It must add no footprint in OrcaSlicer's files.
   - Rewind: "the user will be able to rewind to everything right before the switch, even if the unsaved setting changes were dropped."

   **Latest request (teammate relaying Kenneth), in progress**
   Test what the AI model is sent on the next turn after a profile switch drops setting changes. Kenneth assumes the AI sets settings, and after a switch "the AI should guide the user from the new starting point".
   - Case to run, for a printer switch and separately a filament switch:
     1. The AI changes an object-related setting (e.g. more walls), so the history holds the tool call and its result.
     2. Switch from the header; the change is dropped with no question.
     3. The person asks "is the part still set up to be strong?". Capture the full request.
   - Report, quoting the captured text:
     - What tells the model the printer or filament changed, and where (state section, input tags, activity entry, tool history).
     - What the request says the value is now, and whether anything says the earlier change is no longer in effect. Say plainly whether the request contradicts the earlier "applied" result or leaves it standing.
     - What the default model answers over a few runs, with the count that got it right and the cost.
   - "This is a test and a report, not a fix. If the model is not told, say so and stop: do not change the prompt or the state text without Kenneth's word."
   - Memory rule: ask Kenneth before spending on evals.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Taking OrcaSlicer's messages.** OrcaMessages takes them; MessageRoutes sends them to chat entries via `AgentHost::begin_work`/`finish_work`. WorkFeed tracks upload entries and `fail_upload` ends them; `PrintIssueMonitor::refresh_now` syncs synchronously.
   - **Save-first.** `ShellController::save_before_dropping_changes` calls `m_autosave->save_now()` or reports via `report_unexpected_error`. `answer_unsaved_changes` uses it inside the modal hook.
   - **`OrcaMessages::SavedFirst`.** An RAII scope: the switch saves before the state changes, and the question then does not save again.
   - **Filament switch ordering.** The sidebar sequence (`SetupCommands::select_filament_preset`) calls `set_filament_preset` before `Tab::select_preset`. Printer and process switches ask first.
   - **Version history.** `ProjectAutosave::history()`, `current_version()`, `restore()`, `open_managed_project()`.
     - The LeftPane Versions view lists every version except the current one, newest first.
     - Each row is labelled with `local_time` ("%x %H:%M") plus a "Restore" button whose label is "Restore <time>".
     - `set_restore_confirmation`.
   - **Restore load.** `load_managed_checkpoint` calls `Plater::load_files`, then `PresetBundle::load_config_file_config` and `load_external_preset`. The restore marks the printer dirty in `thumbnails`/`machine_max_junction_deviation`.

     - Script format: `{"answers":[...], "conversations":[{"name","fixture":"single|overhang|plates","plateType","steps":[{"say","replies":[{"call","arguments","record"} | {"text"}]}]}]}`.
     - Templates include `{{result/sessionId}}`, `{{result/revision}}`, `{{workspace/sessionId}}`, `{{workspace/revision}}`, `{{workspace/filamentPreset}}`, `{{workspace/printerPreset}}`.
   - **The app's own request log.** The app logs requests to `<data dir>/jusprin/request-log/*.json`.
   - **What the model is told about a patch.** The settings_apply_patch tool description says: "Without persistAs the change is part of this project: it is kept with the project and used when it slices". This is relevant to the report.
   - **Default model.** Per memory, "slicer-basic = DeepSeek V4 Flash" (via OpenRouter in tests/project_prompt).

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered, with one
  exception below.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

Two kinds of change are ever answered, each only in a case that says so
(`later`), because what matters there is what the model does next: a
`setup_record` with a plan and no purpose (`print-this-no-purpose` and

# What the AI model is sent after a profile switch drops its changes

Commit `3dee824967` on branch `claude/orca-messages-c67fbe` (not merged, not
pushed) adds a step to the prompt recorder (`JusPrinShellHarness
--project-prompt-requests`). In that step the person switches printer or
filament from the header. Nothing in the app or the prompt changed. No model
was called: every request below was recorded from the real app with scripted
model output, at no API cost.

## Short answer

The model is not told. After a printer switch drops the AI's wall-loops
change, the only difference in the next request is one name, in the
`<workspace>` tag on the person's message: `"printerPreset":"Second printer"`
where the earlier turn said `"Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle"`. Nothing says
a switch happened, that changes were dropped, or what any value is now. The
earlier tool result, `"applied":true` with `wall_loops` `2 → 5`, stays in the
history and nothing contradicts it.

## The cases

Each conversation starts on a 20 mm box, X1 Carbon, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm
Standard. Turn 1: "make this part stronger". The model, scripted, previews and
applies a patch, then says what it did. Then the person switches from the
header and asks "is the part still set up to be strong?". The request for that
turn is recorded.

| Case | What the AI changed | Switch | Value after the switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | process `wall_loops` 2 → 5 | printer, to a second saved printer from the same X1 Carbon profile | `wall_loops` 2: dropped |
| B | process `wall_loops` 2 → 5 | filament, to Generic PLA | `wall_loops` 5: kept |
| C | filament `nozzle_temperature` 220 → 230 | filament, to Generic PLA | Generic PLA's 220: dropped |

A filament switch drops only the filament's unsaved changes. The process
change in case B is still in effect, so for B the history happens to be true.
Cases A and C are the ones that matter.

## What the request holds (case A, quoted)

The request has seven input items: the first message, the preview call and its
result, the apply call and its result, the model's reply, and the new message.
The system instructions are the same text as on the earlier turn, byte for
byte, and hold no project state.

- The apply result from turn 1, unchanged in the history:
  `"result":{"applied":true,"changes":[{"after":"5","before":"2","key":"wall_loops"}],...`
  and `"presetDeltas":[{"display":"2 → 5",...,"key":"wall_loops","label":"Wall loops",...,"value":"5"}]`
- The model's own reply from turn 1: "I raised the wall loops from 2 to 5.
  More walls make the part stronger."
- The new message: "is the part still set up to be strong?" followed by
  `<workspace>{"filamentPreset":"Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C",...,"printerPreset":"Second printer","processPreset":"0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C",...}</workspace>`

Here is where each kind of signal stands:

- **State section:** none. The instructions carry no state.
- **Input tags:** the `<workspace>` tag shows the new printer name and nothing
  else. It carries no setting values and no changed-settings list. The process
  name is the same as before, so nothing hints that the process lost a change.
- **Activity entry:** none in the request. The app adds activity rows for the
  switch in the chat the person sees, but they are not sent.
- **Tool history:** the turn-1 "applied" result stands, uncontradicted.

Case C is the same: the tag's `"filamentPreset"` changes from `"Bambu PLA
Basic @BBL X1C"` to `"Generic PLA"`. The history still holds `"applied":true`
with `nozzle_temperature` `"220,220"` → `"230,230"` and the display
`220 → 230 ℃`.

## What the model would learn if it looked

Recorded at the same point with the app's real answers:

- `workspace_inspect` (all sections) lists the new printer and filament
  names. Its `activities` list holds only the AI's two calls ("Preview
  settings", "Change 1 settings of "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C": wall_loops"),
  both `succeeded`. It mentions no switch.
- `settings_get` of `wall_loops` returns the true value: `"value":"2"`,
  `"differsFromPreset":false` in case A, and `"5"`, `"differsFromPreset":true`
  in case B. In case C, `nozzle_temperature` on Generic PLA returns `"220"`.

So a model that reads the setting gets the right value. Nothing prompts it to
read, and the history says the change was applied.

## Not done: the default model's answers

The brief asked what the default model (DeepSeek V4 Flash) answers over a few
runs. That needs a live batch, which Kenneth approves batch by batch, so none
was run.

## Decision needed

Should I run the default model on these recorded requests? The batch is cases
A and C (the two where a change was dropped), 3 runs each, DeepSeek V4 Flash on
the pinned hosts through `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`. Each
request is about 13,000 tokens. A run whose model reads the workspace or a
setting gets up to three more requests with the app's recorded answers. That is
at most 24 requests and about 310,000 input tokens, mostly cached, roughly the
size of the 2026-10-21 batch Kenneth approved (304,272 input tokens). I would
read the six answers myself, with no judge calls. Wiring the two cases into
the runner costs nothing. The other option is to skip the batch and decide on
what the request holds, which already shows the model is not told. I'd run the
batch: whether the model reads `wall_loops` before answering decides how much
the missing signal matters.

## Files

- Script and recordings: scratchpad of this session,
  `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-orca-messages-c67fbe/957f4d29-c627-4dec-b167-0ba8fef2d8b7/scratchpad/switchtest/`
  (`script2.json`, `out2.json` with the requests and the reads' answers,
  `reqlog2/` with the app's own request log).

| Case | The AI changed | Switch | After the switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | wall loops 2 → 5 | printer | 2 (dropped) |

def answers_for(name, step, refused=None, done=(), plan=None, answering=None):
    """The results the app would give the calls of one response, in order,
    or None when one the app would run has no recorded answer. As the app
    does, a refused call (refused: its index and result) gets the refusal,
    and a call after one that did not succeed is answered without being
    run. Reads come from the point after what the run has done (done), with
    the model's plan if it wrote one (plan: its arguments). answering is the
    index among the calls of the change the case asked to have answered: it
    and every read after it are answered from the point after that change."""
    later = CASES[name].later
    point = later.get(done, name)
    results, failed = [], None
    for index, read in enumerate(step.each_read()):
        if failed:
            results.append(not_run(failed))
            continue
        if refused and index == refused[0]:
            results.append(refused[1])
            failed = read
            continue
        if index == answering:
            point = later[done + (read.tool,)]
            plan = read.arguments if read.tool == "setup_record" else plan
            answer = last_output(point)
        else:
            answer = recorded_answer(point, read)
        if answer is None:
            return None, read
        results.append(answer if plan is None else with_plan(point, answer, plan))
        if json.loads(answer).get("state") != "succeeded":
            failed = read
    return results, None


def last_output(point):
    """The last call's result in a recorded request, byte for byte."""
    return next(item["output"] for item in reversed(REQUESTS[point]["body"]["input"])
                if item.get("type") == "function_call_output")


def opening_items(point):
    """What a recorded request appends after the last assistant message: how
    the app opens a turn it starts itself."""
    items = REQUESTS[point]["body"]["input"]
    last = max(index for index, item in enumerate(items) if item.get("role") == "assistant")
    return items[last + 1:]


def run_once(name, instructions, key, model, endpoint, providers):
    def respond(input):
        response = post(body_for(name, instructions, model, providers, input), key, endpoint)
        count(response.get("usage"))
        return response.get("output", [])
    return run_steps(name, respond)


def run_once_claude(name, instructions, model, effort, keep=None):
    """run_once on the Claude Code CLI: the recorded request goes in once, as
    claude_cli.py describes, and each answered read reaches the model as its
    calls' tool results."""
    def start(items):
        return claude_cli.Run(instructions, REQUESTS[name]["body"].get("tools", TOOLS), items, model, effort, keep)

    try:
        runs = [start(REQUESTS[name]["body"]["input"])]
    except Exception as error:  # as a failed request: a failed run, reported as such
        return FAIL, f"ERROR {error}", []

    def respond(_input):
        output, usage = runs[-1].next_response()
        count(usage)
        return output

    # The CLI's run ends with the model's reply, so a new turn is a new run
    # from the whole chat so far.
    def new_turn(input):
        runs[-1].close()
        runs.append(start(input))

    try:
        return run_steps(name, respond, lambda step, results: runs[-1].answer(step.calls, results), new_turn)
    finally:
        runs[-1].close()


def run_steps(name, respond, deliver=lambda step, results: None, new_turn=lambda input: None):
    """One run of a case: respond(input) is the model's output for the
    request so far, deliver(step, results) hands it its reads' results, and
    new_turn(input) says the app has started a turn on input."""
    input = list(REQUESTS[name]["body"]["input"])
    path = []  # the reads answered, one entry per response, for the report
    refusals = 0
    done = ()  # the changes answered and turns started so far (Case.later)
    plan = None  # the arguments of the plan answered, once it is
    try:
        for _ in range(MAX_READS + 4):
            log = [line for line in map(readable, input) if line]
            step = Step(respond(input))
            # A call the app refuses is never judged, read or change: the
            # case sees only the calls before it, and with none the turn
            # simply goes on with the refusal as that call's result.
            refused = first_refused(name, step)
            view = step if refused is None else step.before(refused[0])
            verdict, detail = (CONTINUE, str(step)) if refused and not view.calls else \
                judge_response(CASES[name](REQUESTS[name], log, done), view)
            if verdict == NEXT_TURN:
                path.append(SLICE_END)
                done += (SLICE_END,)
                input += step.output + opening_items(CASES[name].later[done])
                new_turn(input)
                continue
            if verdict not in (CONTINUE, ANSWER_CHANGE):
                break
            answering = view.index if verdict == ANSWER_CHANGE else None
            results, missing = answers_for(name, step, refused, done, plan, answering)
            # MAX_READS counts responses of reads, so the path entries an
            # answered change and a new turn leave do not count against it.
            if results is None or (verdict == CONTINUE and len(path) == MAX_READS + len(done)):
                verdict = UNOBSERVED
                detail = (f"no recorded answer for {missing}" if results is None else f"still reading after answers: {step}")
                break

                    break
            path.append(" + ".join(call["name"] + (" (refused)" if refused and index == refused[0] else "")
                                   for index, call in enumerate(step.calls)))
            deliver(step, results)
            if answering is not None:
                done += (view.tool,)
                plan = view.arguments if view.tool == "setup_record" else plan

            # and its picture included (fe70eea593), the model's output, then
            # a result for every call, in the order the calls were written.

        return FAIL, f"ERROR {error}", [line for line in map(readable, input) if line]

    return verdict, prefix + detail, log + ["model: " + str(step)] + (["model said: " + step.reply] if step.reply and step.tool else [])

"""Sends the recorded after-switch requests to the default model through the
repository's prompt runner (tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py): same
model, hosts, instructions, tools and read answering. Replies are kept whole
for reading by hand; no judge is called."""
import json, os, pathlib, sys

REPO = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
RECORDING = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
OUT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[3])
CASES = sys.argv[4].split(",")
RUNS = int(sys.argv[5])

sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "tests/project_prompt"))
import run_prompt_tests as rpt  # noqa: E402

recording = json.loads(RECORDING.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
for name in CASES:
    request = recording["cases"][name]
    for answer in request["answers"]:
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        if answer.pop("settingItems", False):
            for field in ("items", "unknownKeys"):
                if field in output["result"]:
                    output["result"][field] = [recording["settingItems"][i] for i in output["result"][field]]
        if answer.pop("sharedWorkspace", False):
            output.update(request["sharedWorkspace"])
        answer["output"] = rpt.dump(output)
    rpt.REQUESTS[name] = request

replies = []


class AfterSwitch(rpt.Case):
    def check(self, step):
        if step.tool:
            return (rpt.FAIL if step.changes() else rpt.CONTINUE), str(step)
        replies.append(step.reply)
        return rpt.PASS, "reply"


for name in CASES:
    rpt.CASES[name] = type(name, (AfterSwitch,), {"name": name})

key = os.environ[rpt.KEY_ENV]
instructions = rpt.render()
results = []
for name in CASES:
    for run in range(RUNS):
        replies.clear()
        verdict, detail, log = rpt.run_once(name, instructions, key, rpt.MODEL, rpt.ENDPOINT, rpt.PROVIDERS)
        results.append({"case": name, "run": run + 1, "verdict": verdict, "detail": detail,
                        "reply": replies[-1] if replies else None, "log_tail": log[-6:]})
        print(f"{name} run {run + 1}: {verdict} {detail[:200]}", file=sys.stderr)
        OUT.write_text(json.dumps({"results": results, "usage": rpt.USAGE}, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
print(json.dumps(rpt.USAGE), file=sys.stderr)

Kenneth approved the batch on 2026-11-18 ("Run the batch"): cases A and C,

app's recorded answer at that point.

was right: 4 of 4.** The other 2 runs ended before a reply, for reasons of the
test, not the model. Nothing in the request told the model to check; it
checked on its own.

|---|---|---|

content.text:
For a filament switch, yes. For a printer switch, no. My first answer missed the filament note because my test skipped it.

**Filament switch from the header:** when the person closes the filament menu, the app adds a grey line to the chat (`StatusRow::on_filament_visit`). On the next turn it goes to the model as a developer message, placed after the person's words:

```json
{"role": "developer", "content": "Filament is now Generic PLA. Heat and cooling follow PLA; walls and infill unchanged. Slice again when ready."}
```

It says what the new filament is and that heat and cooling now follow it. It does not say that the AI's own 230 °C change was dropped. The history still shows that change as `"applied":true`.

**Printer switch from the header:** nothing is posted. The printer menu only refreshes the header (`PrinterMenu.cpp:205`). The request has no developer message, and the only sign of the switch is the new printer name in the `<workspace>` tag.

**What was wrong in my test, and what I fixed:**
- My test step switched the filament directly and never closed the menu, so the note was never posted. My earlier filament recordings lacked it, and so did the 3 filament runs in the batch you approved.
- Commit `b8f6c163fa` makes the step end the menu visit the way the menu does. I recorded all three cases again: both filament cases now carry the note above, and the printer case is unchanged.
- I corrected the report to match.
- The printer-switch runs were sent exactly as the app sends them, so their result stands: 3 of 3 read wall loops and found 2.
- The filament runs show the model without the note. They do not show what the real app's request produces.

The report is at `/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_12d59087-ff61-4160-bc55-ec2a878865f9/switch-next-turn-request-report.md`.
